releases.notes:

the next release; you get that release as a normal update.

## Please test

New: GRID Legends starts (OBB disk images, experimental), eye-tracked foveation centred for games that render only part of their image (In Death, The 7th Guest), 'Ignore the laser pointer' for flat apps with 'Controllers as a gamepad', the GL shim chooses multiview automatically again.

- Ignore the laser pointer: bind /dev/null at Waydroid's pointer pipe (#162)
- Controllers as a gamepad: option to ignore the laser pointer (#162)
- Foveation: re-base Valve's gaze offset on the pass's render area, not the framebuffer (#394, #520: eye-tracked sharp area pulled toward each rect's centre in

- OBB disk images: open GRID's Index.txt in the images' spelling (#308)
- Catalog: Alex (MR not working yet, #588) and Sushi Ben (frog voice distorts, #584) as issues

- Agent v128: the Files tab's saves and move commands on top of main's v127 (#532)

- Settings → Artwork: optional SteamGridDB API key; picker failure messages
- Artwork fallbacks when the Meta services are down (#510)
- a32 bridge: __gnu_Unwind_Find_exidx finds the guest library's unwind table, not the runtime's (#439)
- Agent v127: OBB disk-image unpacking (#308) on top of v126's device features
- OBB disk images: hand the mounted path over from the caller's allocator instead of patching GRID's code (#308)
- OBB disk images: GRID frees the mounted path with its own allocator; skip that free
- OBB disk images: unpack on the Frame instead of mounting (#308, GRID Legends)
- adapter.fixed_resolution: also hold Unity's viewport at full size and rebuild the APK (#574)
- Catalog: JKXR works with gl_error_clear; cinematics need the GL state guard (#441, #502)
- Tests and lint after merging the device, FrameBridge round-2, stable-id and Horizon branches
- frame.horizon_platform_stub: local HorizonPlatformCore for Meta's Horizon Platform SDK, no licence answers (#511)
- frame.stable_android_id: the same Android device id at every start (#420)
- apk: small dex writer for generated helper classes (dexgen), Dex descriptor/find_string helpers
- device.offline: block new outbound connections in the container's netns (nft via podman unshare nsenter) instead of --network=none; PON reasons in kernel 6.18
- Steam's language by default, offline games, an extra Frame folder, power-loss restarts (agent v126)
- FrameBridge: keep a GLES game's GL bindings across the runtime's calls (gl_state_guard, #441/#502)
- FrameBridge: performance levels, RGBA8 formats, per-eye poses, detached syncs, haptics summary, stale waits, controller battery (#336, #400, #527, #476, #567,

releases.name: FramePort v1.4.0
releases.notes:
FramePort v1.4.0: Windows (x64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux (x64, ARM64).

## What's new

- **Games are paused before they close**, as on a Quest, also with Steam's Exit game, so saves written on pause are kept.
- **App bundles:** .xapk, .apks, .apkm and split-APK folders install as one app; expansion files with a download's copy suffix get the name the game looks for.
- **Menus:** FramePort's own right-click and "…" menus with submenus; long items wrap at any scale.
- **Typing window:** SteamVR's theater mode no longer takes the controllers from games that show their Android window.
- **New options:** shared folders between two games (JKXR's companion app), sign-in pages from apps that look for a browser (Plex), space warp for games that require it, and an opt-in switch into VR for hybrid apps (YouTube).
- **Game fixes:** The Climb 1/2 start again, AC Nexus runs as a Quest 3, Ghost Giant's intro videos, QuestZDoom's slowdown, Asgard's Wrath 2's data files, Just Dance VR's offline save, Eleven Table Tennis' Meta sign-in, Xelee, YouTube's start crash, and games that quit on a refused refresh rate. 10-bit video decodes in software (thanks @Veticia).
- **Fixes:** Windows updates never mix two versions, folder names with ® or accents when FramePort runs on Linux or the Frame, FramePort on the Frame links game data instead of copying it twice, diagnostics include SteamVR's logs, AUR install notes (thanks @lucasoskorep).
- **33 new recipes.**

If FramePort doesn't start after updating from 1.3.0 on Windows, unpack the new `FramePort-windows-x64.zip` into an empty folder; games and settings are kept.

Already have FramePort? It offers this update itself (Library → **Update now**).

## Install

Download the file for your PC, unpack it and start FramePort. Guide:
[Install and first steps](https://frameport.app/docs/install/).

- **Controllers:** an experimental Quest button mode, and own button layouts for the gamepad in 2D apps.
- **Game fixes:** Batman: Arkham Shadow's edge line and audio hooks (thanks @Lucas-Mathieu), PrimedGun, 4XVR's menus, Halo CE VR closing during the intro, OutRun, Transformers Beyond Reality, cube loading screens, and Unreal games whose install stopped at a memory patch check.

- **Fixes:** uploads with OpenSSH work with "[" or "]" in a folder name, "Update with a newer version…" for Linux apps and PC VR games, and Settings shows the options most people use first.

- **Fixed: games missing from the Frame's Steam library** ("Game configuration unavailable"): every Steam account gets the game, FramePort checks it's still there after Steam restarts, and Play adds a missing game by itself.

releases.name: FramePort v0.4.0
releases.notes:
FramePort v0.4.0: Windows (x64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux (x64).

## What's new

- **Game settings**: picture, controllers, menus, 360° video and mixed-reality options in plain words, only the ones that matter for each game; kept with the game and applied on the Frame right away.
- **Customize** describes every patch in plain words; **Show technical details** adds the exact effects.
- **Install queue**: waits for the Frame when it sleeps or drops off the Wi-Fi and continues where it stopped; keeps the Frame awake while installing; checks free space before large batches; **Update all** asks each question once for all games.
- **Ordinary Android apps** (no VR) run as a flat window in the headset, with Android's navigation buttons hidden; they get a cover and icon from the APK.
- **Files tab** for videos, documents, mods and saves on the Frame (upload, download, rename, delete, multi-select).
- **Share how a game runs**: untested games ask whether they work, so working recipes can join the built-in catalog.
- **Clearer errors** for common problems (Frame offline, disk full, game running, damaged APK).
- Your game files are never changed; the converted copies are temporary.
- Fixes: picked artwork is kept (and Meta store picks use the shown picture); already converted games aren't converted twice (Wallace & Gromit, Espire 2); library search and name sorting; the page no longer jumps while changing patches or reading the install log; Proton test "Connect failed"; notifications close themselves and have an X; larger default window.

Already have FramePort? It offers this update itself (Library → **Update now**, or `frameport update`).

## First launch

The builds are signed with a free self-signed certificate (Windows) and an ad-hoc signature (macOS), so the first
start shows a warning:

- **Windows:** "Windows protected your PC" → **More info** → **Run anyway**. Optional: import
  `FramePort-selfsigned.cer` (attached to each release) into *Trusted Root Certification Authorities* (Current User) to
  show FramePort as the publisher; the certificate can only sign code. Remove it with `certmgr.msc`.
- **macOS:** right-click `FramePort.app` → **Open** → **Open** (once), or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine FramePort.app`.
- **Linux:** `tar xzf FramePort-linux-x64.tar.gz && ./FramePort/FramePort`.

## Connecting the Steam Frame

1. On the Frame: Settings → System → Developer → turn on **Developer Mode**. The Frame and the computer must be on the
   same network.
2. In FramePort open **Steam Frame**. A Frame in Developer Mode appears in the list.
3. First time only: on the Frame switch to Desktop mode (Steam button → Power → Switch to Desktop), open Konsole and
   run the command FramePort shows. It enables SSH, authorises this computer and installs Valve's Android runtime
   (Lepton) if needed.

## Installing games

- **Install on Frame** on a game's page (or select several in the Library and install them together). Installs run
  one after another in the background; **Activity** shows the current one at the top.
- **Update all** reinstalls every game whose build changed (e.g. after a FramePort update). Questions that need an
  answer (e.g. Oculus games that can't run on the Frame) are asked once, for all games.
- If the Frame goes to sleep, turns off or leaves the Wi-Fi, the queue **waits** and continues once it's back; uploads
  pick up where they stopped. While installs run, FramePort keeps the Frame from going to sleep. Before a large batch
  it checks the Frame has enough free space.
- Your own game files are never changed. The converted copy is temporary: it's removed once the game is on the Frame
  (Settings → Installing: keep them, or remove all now).
- **Game settings…** (game menu or the Steam Frame page): sharpness, refresh rate, controllers, menus, 360° video and
  mixed-reality options in plain words, only those that matter for the game. Changes are kept with the game and,
  when it's installed, used the next time it starts.
- Ordinary Android apps (no VR) are installed unchanged and shown as a flat window in the headset. Android's
  back/home/recents buttons are hidden by default (patch **Hide Android's navigation bar**).

## Updating

FramePort checks for a new release at start and every 6 hours (it only downloads the release information). When one
exists, the Library shows **Update now**: FramePort downloads the new version, verifies it against the release's
`SHA256SUMS.txt` (on Windows also the signature), restarts and opens as the new version. Games, settings, signing keys
and the Frame connection are kept. Running installs finish first. **Later** skips that version.

Settings → **Updates**: turn the check off, or turn on **Install updates automatically** (downloads in the background,
installs at the next start). If FramePort's folder isn't writable, **Update now** opens the release page instead. The
update log is `logs/update.log` in the data folder.

Command line: `frameport update` (`--check` only checks, exit code 10 = update available; `--yes` doesn't ask).
`FRAMEPORT_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` turns all checks off.

## PC VR games

PC VR games are Windows VR games (OpenXR, SteamVR or Oculus). Scan a folder of them (one folder per game) or use
**Add games → Add one game folder…**. FramePort finds the game's program and asks when there is more than one
candidate. **Already patched** on a game page installs a copy unchanged. Oculus-only games need Revive: FramePort uses
an installed Revive, or downloads a portable copy.

- **Play from this PC:** Windows with Steam and SteamVR. **Install on this PC** adds the game to Steam; stream it to the
  Frame with Steam Link. If a game can't keep up with the refresh rate, FramePort lowers the rate and enables motion
  smoothing in SteamVR's per-game settings the next time you press Play.
- **Play on the Frame (experimental):** Steam Frame → *PC VR games (Proton)* → **Install**, then **Install on Frame**
  on the game page.
- Games that use the Oculus Platform SDK check the licence through the Oculus app, so they run on the PC only.

## Files on the Frame (videos, documents, mods, saves)

The **Files** tab manages files on the Frame over the same connection as installs; no other transfer app is needed.
Pick a location, browse folders, and use **Upload files** / **Upload folder**, **New folder**, or the download, rename
and delete buttons on each entry. Tick several entries (or the box above the list for all) to download or delete them
together. In the downloaded app you can also drag files and folders from Explorer / Finder / your file manager onto
the list to upload them into the open folder. Uploads and downloads run in the Activity panel, resume after an interruption and
skip files that are already there.

- **Videos**, **Downloads** and **Documents** appear inside every Quest game as `/sdcard/Movies`, `/sdcard/Download`
  and `/sdcard/Documents`. Apps find files by browsing folders; Android's media index doesn't work on the Frame.
- Under **Game storage**, each installed game has its own `/sdcard` (mods, saves). A game's menu → **Add videos and
  files…** opens it. Video players that list only their own folder (e.g. 4XVR's "Internal Storage" = `4XPlayer`) find
  videos uploaded into that folder.
- **Home folder** shows everything in the Frame's home folder (hidden files with **Show hidden files**).

Command line: `frameport frame send <files> --dest videos` (`frameport frame storage` lists the destinations).

## Sharing a working game, reporting a problem

- **Share working config…** (game menu): opens a prefilled GitHub issue with the game's patches and settings. Accepted
  configs become built-in recipes. Untested games ask on their page once they've been installed or tested: **It
  works**, **It has issues** or **It doesn't run**.
- **Report a problem…** (game menu, or Settings → Problems and feedback): saves a diagnostics zip to Documents (logs,
  recipe, device details; IP addresses, user names, home folders and Steam ids replaced) and opens a prefilled GitHub
  issue to attach it to. Command line: `frameport diag report <game>`, `frameport share-recipe <game>`.

## Command line

Everything the app does is also a `frameport` command (in a source checkout: `uv run frameport`); `frameport --help`
and `frameport <command> --help` describe every option. The main ones:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `scan <folder>` / `list` / `show <game>` | add games, list the library, show a game's analysis and patches |
| `recipe <game> --enable/--disable <patch>` | change a game's patches (`patches` lists them all) |
| `build <game>` / `install <game>` / `test <game>` | build, install on the Frame (`--to pc` for PC VR on this PC), launch test |
| `frame discover` / `frame connect` / `frame info` | find, pair with and describe the Frame |
| `frame send` / `frame storage` / `frame cleanup` | copy files to the Frame, show where they go, free space |
| `tools status` / `tools install` | the tools FramePort downloads |
| `diag report <game>` / `share-recipe <game>` | report a problem / share a working recipe |
| `update` | update FramePort |

Exit codes: 0 done, 1 something failed, 2 wrong usage, 10 (`update --check`) a newer version exists. Errors are
one line on stderr; `FRAMEPORT_DEBUG=1` shows the full traceback.

## Uninstalling

Settings → **Uninstall FramePort…** (or `frameport uninstall-app`) removes its data folder, the Steam shortcuts it
added on this computer and, optionally, its games on the Frame (saves can be kept). It first saves your signing keys
to Documents: game updates must be signed with the same key. Then delete the program folder.

## Verify a download

Each archive has a GitHub build attestation:
`gh attestation verify FramePort-windows-x64.zip -R spoopyghosty0/frameport`. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists the checksums
(`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt`). Windows certificate SHA-256 fingerprint:
`4E:12:98:91:62:C0:E4:50:FB:65:1D:34:BB:73:00:09:7B:78:BE:88:5C:A7:6C:42:23:46:9B:92:A1:59:A7:6E`.

1. On the Frame: Settings → System → Developer → turn on **Developer Mode**. The Frame and the computer must be on the
   same network.
2. In FramePort open **Steam Frame**. A Frame in Developer Mode appears in the list.
3. First time only: on the Frame switch to Desktop mode (Steam button → Power → Switch to Desktop), open Konsole and
   run the command FramePort shows. It enables SSH, authorises this computer and installs Valve's Android runtime
   (Lepton) if needed.

## Updating

FramePort checks for a new release at start and every 6 hours (it only downloads the release information). When one
exists, the Library shows **Update now**: FramePort downloads the new version, verifies it against the release's

line: `frameport frame send <files> --to videos`.

  configs become built-in recipes.

  recipe, device details; IP addresses, user names, home folders and Steam ids replaced) and opens a prefilled GitHub

to Documents: game updates must be signed with the same key. Then delete the program folder.
